_meta.purpose: What is computed for each information need from the tests linked to it. Every indicator is one of three fixed templates applied to one variable; this file only chooses the variable, the filter and the grouping. An indicator describes what was recorded. Its 'reading' says what it does not mean. Nothing here is a NASA result; where a published result exists for the same investigation, 'compare_with' points to it in references.json.

templates.summary: number of tests with a value, and the listed statistics (min, median, max) of the variable
templates.count_by: number of tests for each value of the variable
templates.count: number of tests that pass the filter

population.usable: tests counted for the need: they meet its required conditions, hold an outcome, and their investigation is linked to the need by a 'stated_by' entry with verdict 'supported'
population.recorded: tests that meet the required conditions and hold an outcome, whatever the link; used where the tests behind an indicator are outside the stated objective, and the reading says so
population.in_scope: tests within the need's scope that hold every required condition, with or without an outcome, from the investigations linked to the need with verdict 'supported'

_meta.where: filters as [variable, operator, value]; operators: ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=, notnull, contains
_meta.removed: P1.lowest_flow_listed_at_extinction was removed on 2026-11-14: 12 of its 14 values came from cells that say the flow went lower than the number written, so the value was not the flow at extinction.

indicators.label: Initial oxygen of the tests run
indicators.reading: The range of initial oxygen over which this material and shape was tested. Not a flammability limit: a test at an oxygen level does not by itself show that the sample burned or went out there. For the Saffire tests the value is the oxygen the ISS reported when the vehicle departed, about one day before the tests, carried forward from the CO2 produced (SAF17.o2_initial_I, SAF17.o2_initial_II, SAF17.table1_note_i, PSISAF.delay); it is not a sensor reading at ignition. Of the Saffire tests only those of Saffire-II are counted for this need. Where a Saffire cell holds two numbers, the value is the one the investigators name as the initial oxygen; a cell for which no publication names it has no value here, and no midpoint is computed.

indicators.label: Initial oxygen of tests in which the oxygen reading fell
indicators.reading: Tests whose final oxygen reading is below the initial reading. No threshold is put on the size of the fall, and a fall does not by itself show that the sample burned: some falls are 0.1 point, and one such test is noted "would not stay lit" in the table. The minimum is the lowest initial oxygen of such a test in this table, not the limiting oxygen concentration.

indicators.label: Events noted next to the flow settings
indicators.reading: Number of tests in which the table notes an event word beside the flow or fan settings: extinction, blowoff, no ignition or not sustained. The absence of a word does not mean that the flame did not go out: the investigators report that the flames always quenched when the fan was turned off (ICES19.fanoff), and cells that end in "off" carry no event word. Extinction at low flow and blowoff at high flow are the two branches of the flammability boundary (ICES19.boundary).

indicators.label: Initial oxygen of tests with a noted flow event
indicators.reading: Oxygen at the start of the tests in which the table notes an event (extinction, blowoff, no ignition, not sustained). It is the starting value, not the oxygen at the event; the oxygen after the test is in 'P1.o2_after_extinction'.

indicators.label: Oxygen after the test, in tests with an extinction noted
indicators.reading: Final oxygen reading of the tests in which the table notes an extinction. The BASS-II investigators write that the sensors served 'to determine oxygen depletion, extinction oxygen concentrations, and the completeness of combustion' (ICES19.sensors); taking the final reading of a test with an extinction noted as that oxygen is the team's step. Each value belongs to one test at its own flow setting, and in many of these tests the flame went out as the flow was lowered; a value here is not the lowest oxygen at which the material burns. Tests whose final reading is above the initial reading or implausibly low have no value and carry a flag.

indicators.label: Flame spread rate in microgravity
indicators.reading: Spread rate as written in the table. Cells with text instead of a number are not counted. Among the mapped tables only the Saffire-II table (PSI-99) has a spread-rate column, and the Saffire-II tests are not counted for this need (link verdict 'differs', SAF16b.saffire2); the values shown here come from those tests, which are recorded outside the stated objective and are not counted for this need. The published rates of SAF.result are for Saffire-I, whose table has no spread-rate column.

indicators.label: Length burned in microgravity
indicators.reading: Burn length as written in the column "?-g Burn Length" of the Saffire-II table (first character unreadable in the PSI file). Cells written "~ 0" are read as 0. Two PMMA cells, "~ 10 cm (note 3)" and "~ 10 cm (note 4)", are read as 10 and carry the flag burn_length_cm:see_note_in_source; Note 3 of the table says "This is the length of fuel with significant visible damage." The cell "5 cm & 0 (note 2)" gives no value. The 15 cm criterion of NASA-STD-6001B Test 1 is defined for a 30 cm specimen in normal gravity without air flow; these tests were not run under that standard and are not judged against it. The Saffire-II tests are not counted for this need (link verdict 'differs', SAF16b.saffire2); the values shown here come from those tests, which are recorded outside the stated objective and are not counted for this need.

indicators.label: Burn time
indicators.reading: Burn time as written in the table. In the current outputs the values are those of the Saffire-I tests (PSI-98). A burn time is not a spread rate; using it as an outcome of this need is the team's choice.

indicators.label: How the tests ended
indicators.reading: Number of tests by the word in the "Test end" column of the FLEX table: extinction, disruption or completion. The table does not define the words. "Extinction" is how a droplet burn ended, with or without carbon dioxide or helium added; it is not a count of flames put out by an agent.

indicators.label: Initial oxygen by how the test ended
indicators.reading: Range of ambient oxygen of the tests that ended in each way. Tests with carbon dioxide or helium added and tests with neither are in the same group, while the published values (MST14.loi) are given separately for oxygen/nitrogen and for carbon dioxide added: a minimum here is not one of those values. Not the limiting oxygen index: the LOI is found from extinction diameters, which this indicator does not use.

indicators.label: Carbon dioxide added to the atmosphere
indicators.reading: Range of carbon dioxide concentration in the tests where it was added as a suppressant. Not a minimum extinction concentration.

indicators.label: Helium added to the atmosphere
indicators.reading: Range of helium concentration in the tests where it was added. Not a minimum extinction concentration.

indicators.label: Change in the CO reading (final minus initial)
indicators.reading: Final minus initial CO reading of the on-board sensor of the experiment (ICES19.sensors). Not the amount produced by one test: many tests start with a CO reading above zero, and a difference can be negative (flag final_below_initial). Not a cabin concentration: it is not compared with crew exposure limits (SMAC.scope). Tests whose reading was over range are not in this range; see D1.co_over_range. The tests are counted for this need through the investigators' purpose sentence for the gas measurements (BASS2TM.products, ICES15.purpose). The investigators describe the sensors as measuring the completeness of combustion (ICES19.sensors); in the passages read they do not present the readings as a detection measurement.

indicators.label: Tests with the CO reading over range
indicators.reading: Number of tests in which the final CO reading was recorded as over range ("OR", above 1000 ppm per the BASS-II ReadMe). This is a limit of the instrument reading, not a requirement; the upper end of the monitoring range in 3001.T6.2-3 is the same figure, and the pipeline does not relate the two. The tests are counted for this need through the investigators' purpose sentence for the gas measurements (BASS2TM.products, ICES15.purpose). The investigators describe the sensors as measuring the completeness of combustion (ICES19.sensors); in the passages read they do not present the readings as a detection measurement.

indicators.label: Ratio of the change in CO to the change in CO2
indicators.reading: Molar ratio computed by the pipeline (formula in variables.json) from the differences between the final and the initial CO and CO2 readings. A team computation, not the investigators' value. No ratio is computed for a test whose CO reading is over range or missing, whose CO difference is zero or negative, or whose CO2 difference is below 0.05 percentage points. The investigators present the CO/CO2 ratio as a measure of completeness of combustion of interest to the combustion community (BASS2TM.coratio); using it for a detection need is the team's choice. The tests are counted for this need through the investigators' purpose sentence for the gas measurements (BASS2TM.products, ICES15.purpose).

indicators.label: Air flow past the heated sample
indicators.reading: Range of air flow in the smoke tests. Particle sizes, which the flow affects, are not in the PSI tables. The rows hold test conditions; no measured smoke property is in the table. The SAME values (PSI-102) are those of the planned test matrix (SAMEEIRD.matrix); whether tests were flown at exactly these conditions was not verified.

indicators.label: Smoke aging time
indicators.reading: Range of aging time in the smoke tests. Two source columns are read as this one variable: "Aging Duration (minutes)" of the SAME table (PSI-102), multiplied by 60, and "Net aging time (sec)" of the SAME-R table (PSI-101). The SAME-R columns "Primary aging time (sec)" and "Primary mixing time (sec)" are not read. The rows hold test conditions; no measured smoke property is in the table. The SAME values (PSI-102) are those of the planned test matrix (SAMEEIRD.matrix); whether tests were flown at exactly these conditions was not verified.

indicators.label: Target weight loss rate of the planned test matrix
indicators.reading: Value of the column "Weight loss rate (mg/min)" of the SAME table (PSI-102). The requirements document calls these target mass loss rates of the test matrix (SAMEEIRD.target); they are planned values, not measured results, and the mass actually lost is not in the table.
